answer: Agents bind identities to unique juniper trees growing in a canyon oasis by periodically submitting a laser-scanned trunk profile hashed with local humidity sensors and satellite canyon imagery. Duplicate profiles are rejected. An attacker scaling to 30 sybils must secure 30 distinct juniper stands across separate canyon oases plus scanners, incurring land and equipment costs; clustered farms fail the geographic uniqueness test. Honest agents keep one tree for many epochs at low cost. Sensor drift from dust storms is a noted failure mode requiring re-scans.
